body.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
body.justification: This remains the field-tier target: the new sparse-regime converse must still be matched by a total uniformly calibrated omnibus test, and the dense-regime converse and transition boundaries must be completed on the identical class.
body.gap: The lower map now closes for \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but its connected-cluster series fails at the natural scale when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\).  The upper pair-factor architecture is invalidated by the scoped covariance-masking alternative, and no richer full-cell statistic with a deterministic alternative dichotomy and complete occupancy concentration has yet been proved.
body.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying a fitted forest or turning non-rejection into evidence of homogeneity.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a total multiresolution test with a population signal that remains nonzero on the exact covariance-masking alternative, prove uniform finite-sample level and power including every sparse-occupancy projection, and optimize it; extend the constant-null-supported converse to the dense collision regime \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), then compare the independently obtained maps and determine the remaining boundary logarithms.
obligation.obstruction: The new lower construction controls all connected collision clusters when \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but at its natural scale \(nh^d\to\infty\) when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), so the geometric connected-component bound no longer closes.  On the upper side, \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) supplies an original-class alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) and \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin, annihilating the proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population signals.  This is an obstruction to that architecture only; no all-test or all-statistic impossibility is claimed.
obligation.attempted: The sign-conditioned common one-observation marginal was used before comparing the prior predictives.  Component cell probabilities were bounded below by \(1/16\), the atom-moment discrepancy was bounded by \(\delta\), and the bounded-overlap collision graph was summed over labeled spanning trees.  This yields \(H^2\leq Cn^2h^d\delta^2\) and the sparse nuisance lower rate \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\), with no extra outer-sign term.  At the stress tuple the scale was optimized to \(n^{-2/7}\).  A richer full four-cell multinomial score was considered as the next upper route, but no uniform alternative dichotomy and complete concentration proof were obtained in this bounded round.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), and define
\[
 b_n=
 \begin{cases}
 n^{-2\min\{\gamma,s_0\}/(4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}+d)},&d\leq4\min\{\gamma,s_0\},\\
 n^{-4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}/(4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}+3d)},&d>4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The proved all-regime upper bound is \(\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\), and the known-propensity converse gives \(\rho_n^*\geq c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\).  The new sparse-regime null-supported construction additionally proves, whenever \(d\geq2s_0\),
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq c\max\left\{
 n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},
 n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}
 \right\}.
\]
At \(d=2s_0\) this converse has no logarithmic loss.  If \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\), the nuisance term is strictly larger than the known-propensity order and certifies
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \geq c n^{,2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
In particular, at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\),
\[
 c n^{-2/7}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad
 \rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{4/35}.
\]
The previously proved no-penalty region \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\) remains matched, with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  Outside these closed subregions, the lower and upper exponents do not match.  For \(d<2s_0\), the present collision expansion has \(nh_n^d\to\infty\), so connected components of unbounded order are not controlled by its geometric summation.  On the upper side, \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) gives a legal alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) but zero population mean for every proposed statistic containing the specified within-bin covariance factor.  A richer full-cell signal with a uniform deterministic alternative dichotomy, all of its sparse-occupancy projections, and finite-sample calibration has not been constructed.  Thus the independently derived maps are not yet matched, transition logarithms beyond the proved boundaries remain unknown, the frozen \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) remain diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.
